subject: Custom SLA addendum & order form language — Bionova (MSA/SOW attachments)
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@bionova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Cc: Bionova Procurement <procurement@bionova.com>
Date: 2026-10-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA addendum language and order form attachments

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency improvements look promising. Procurement asked me to send a consolidated note about our remaining asks on the MSA and order form so we can close redlines faster. High level:

- We need explicit language in the SLA addendum for scheduled maintenance windows (weekly maintenance windows up to 6 hours/month) and confirmation that these windows will not count toward uptime calculations.
- For production traffic the customer wants a regional latency commitment: 99th percentile p95 latency < 120ms for the US-EAST region when requesting the "low-latency" profile. If Redwood cannot meet that on hosted tiers, we need an order form option for Dedicated Capacity with an alternate credit schedule.
- A clear Service Credit schedule tied to monthly availability bands (example in the attached MSA redline).

I'm attaching a redline of our MSA and a short doc with suggested SLA language. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) add a dedicated order form line for a low-latency profile, and 2) accept the proposed maintenance carve-out?

We'd like to finalize this week if possible.

Best,
Sara Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering
Bionova Therapeutics

Attachments: Bionova_MSA_redline_20261015.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@bionova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-10-15 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum language and order form attachments

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Karthik (sales) for order form/pricing and Soojin (legal) for the MSA language. Quick answers up front:

- Maintenance windows: we can accept an exclusion for scheduled maintenance up to 8 hours/month if the windows are mutually agreed and Redwood provides 72 hours advance notice. We prefer 8 hours as an upper bound to allow for phased rollouts, but can take 6 hours if that's a hard constraint.
- Latency commitment: we need to confirm performance profiles against our hosted pools. If Redwood cannot guarantee 99th p95 < 120ms on hosted, we can include a Dedicated Capacity SKU in the order form which carries the tighter latency SLA and a separate credit schedule.
- Credits: we'll propose a stepped credit schedule (0.5% monthly credit for 99.9-99.5, 2% for 99.5-99.0, etc.) — baseline proposal attached.

Soojin — see Sara's suggested language (attached). Can you comment on acceptability and any additional carve-outs we should add (force majeure, emergency maintenance, telemetry thresholds)?

Sara — I'll put together a short order form line item with Dedicated Capacity and a matching SLA Appendix. Can you confirm the target capacity (approx vCPU/GPU count or QPS) so Karthik can price it?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@bionova.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-10-15 13:41 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum language and order form attachments

Thanks, Kim. Sara — quick commercial note: if Bionova elects the Dedicated Capacity SKU for the low-latency profile we'll price it as a committed monthly bundle (reserved GPUs + baseline throughput). Typical uplift for the latency-backed SKU is ~30-40% above standard hosted per-token economics due to pinned capacity and prioritized routing. We can either: 1) include a line item for a 6-month pilot at a reduced uplift to validate latency, or 2) move to a 12-month commit with deeper discount.

To price, I need an approximate steady-state QPS and your expected average sequence length. If you can provide an estimate tonight I can circulate a draft order form tomorrow morning (will include the SLA Appendix and credit schedule as discussed).

Also confirming: order form will include a clause that Dedicated Capacity's SLA supersedes hosted SLA for the services listed in Appendix A.

Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@bionova.com>
Date: 2026-10-16 09:07 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum language and order form attachments

Sara / team — reviewed Bionova's MSA redline and the SLA draft. A few legal points and suggested edits: 

1) Maintenance carve-out: Acceptable with the following guardrails — 72 hours notice for planned maintenance and a requirement to schedule maintenance outside of Bionova's defined "business-critical" windows (we should add a definition of "business-critical" in Appendix A). Maintenance that exceeds the agreed monthly cap should either be credited or be subject to a remediation plan.

2) Latency slices: We should avoid absolute hard guarantees on p95 across publicly hosted pools; instead we can offer a named "Low-Latency Dedicated Profile" with guaranteed performance on Dedicated Capacity and an acceptance test (30-day soak) to validate latency. The acceptance test should be documented in Appendix B with telemetry hooks and sample prompt sets.

3) Credits: define maximum aggregate credit per 12-month period and a cure period for incidents attributable to upstream cloud provider or force majeure.

4) Evidence & audit: procurement asked for telemetry access — propose an ops-readonly dashboard for Bionova and a monthly tokens/latency report; we can provide limited SRE runbook excerpts but will not share internal oncall rotas.

I will prepare redline language for (a) Appendix A (availability/maintenance definition), (b) Appendix B (acceptance test / telemetry), and (c) the order form clause tying the Dedicated SKU to the SLA. Kimberly/Karthik — I will need to coordinate on the exact credit percentages you want in the order form.

Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Addendum_draft_20261016.docx

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@bionova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-10-17 16:48 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum language and order form attachments

Appreciate the quick turn. A few follow-ups after internal review: 

- Bionova agrees to the 72-hour notice for maintenance but prefers the 6 hours/month cap rather than 8. We can be flexible on scheduling windows if Redwood provides a regular maintenance calendar.
- We're fine with Dedicated Capacity being the vehicle for the low-latency guarantee — we'll start with a 6-month pilot (target start 2027-01-15). Please include a pilot pricing line and an acceptance test described in Appendix B.
- For credits: Procurement asked that the maximum aggregate credit not exceed 10% of the monthly fee; can Redwood confirm this cap is acceptable? If so, we can proceed to DocuSign once order form language is updated.

Next steps: Karthik — please send a one-page pilot order form and a separate SLA Appendix that includes the acceptance test script (we'll need the sample prompt set to run during the soak). Soojin — if you can circulate redlines for Appendix A/B by tomorrow we can align legal and procurement.

Best,
Sara
